text: Das Spiel zwischen Kingsmoor FC und Westport Albion endete mit einem packenden 3:3. Viktor Quinlan zeigte eine starke Leistung und erzielte zwei wichtige Tore, darunter ein Elfmeter in der 8. Minute – eine Chance, die in etwa 8 von 10 Fällen verwandelt wird [#152] [#222]. Westport Albion antwortete schnell mit zwei Treffern von Rafael Delacroix, die aus schnellen Angriffen mit vertikalen Pässen entstanden, was ihre direkte Spielweise gut unterstreicht [#401] [#553]. Nach der Pause erzielte Kenji Rahman den Ausgleich zum 2:2 für Westport, bevor Lucas Iversen für Kingsmoor kurz nach einer roten Karte für Felix Barros traf, um das Ergebnis spannend zu halten [#983] [#1494] [#1516]. Kingsmoor hatte mit 3,06 xG (erwartete Tore; zeigt, wie viele Chancen sie hatten) eine starke Offensive, während Westport mit 3,77 xG fast noch mehr gute Möglichkeiten hatte. Das Spiel war voller Tempowechsel und taktischer Anpassungen, was für viel Spannung sorgte und den Fans ein packendes Erlebnis bescherte.

- Viktor Quinlan scored 2 goals including a penalty at 8' and an open play goal at 12', contributing to Kingsmoor FC's total goals [#152, #222].
- Rafael Delacroix scored twice for Westport Albion at 22' and 30', keeping the match competitive [#401, #553].
- Kenji Rahman scored an equalizer for Westport Albion at 51' to make the score 2-2 [#983].
- A red card was issued to Felix Barros of Kingsmoor FC at 81', impacting the team's defensive strength [#1494, #1495].
- Luca Iversen scored for Kingsmoor FC at 82', narrowing the deficit to 3-2 shortly after the red card [#1516].

- Kingsmoor FC's first goal came from a penalty, reflecting a defensive lapse or foul by Westport Albion leading to a high-value set piece situation early in the match [152]. The quick pace and directness to the penalty taker Viktor Quinlan show their intent to capitalize on any chance against a 4-4-2 structure that plays wide with crossing options.
- Kingsmoor’s second goal at 12' resulted from an 8-pass build-up starting immediately from a ball regain, highlighting an effective counter-attack and quick transition exploiting their 4-4-2 wide formation by involving multiple players, especially wide men like Felix Duarte providing key assists [220,222].
- Westport Albion responded with goals at 22' and 30' through Rafael Delacroix, underpinning their style of direct, vertical passing. Both goals came from relatively short sequences starting from regains, indicating purposeful counter-pressing and efficient use of vertical passes from their 4-4-2 shape to quickly reach scoring positions [399,401,552,553].
- Westport’s goal at 30' was assisted via a cross from Dylan Rahman, pointing to their effective crossing within their direct play style, combined with timely positional support from wide midfielders or overlapping fullbacks [553].
- The equalizer by Westport at 51' shows a shorter passing move starting from a throw-in leading to a cross assist, suggesting focused exploitation of set-piece or throw-in situations as tactical overload spots within their direct style and compact 4-4-2 formation [982,983].
- Kingsmoor’s tactical style of wide crossing play is well represented in their late goal at 82' where Mason Morales’ cross assisted Luca Iversen inside the box after a quick regain in open play, illustrating their reliance on wide areas and crossing into the box in their 4-4-2 [1515,1516].
- The match dynamics shifted with Kingsmoor increasing press intensity, directness, and line height after going behind at 65', reflecting a push to force turnovers high up the pitch and deliver quick attacking transitions typical in a 4-4-2 wide system chasing a comeback [1187].
- Conversely, Westport Albion dropped deeper and slowed tempo around 79' to protect the lead, consistent with a 4-4-2 adapting to game context by reducing risk in vertical passing and pressing intensity, aiming to retain structural compactness [1459].
